claims.claim_ar: نداء بـ«يا» يُحَوِّلُ الخطابَ مباشرةً إلى المخاطَب (هنا: «يا صالح») لتكثيفِ التوجيه والتوبيخ.
claims.claim_en: Vocative with «يا» shifts the discourse directly to the addressee (here: “O Salih”), concentrating the address and reproach.

claims.claim_ar: تكرار العطف بـ«واو» بين الأحداث (فَعَقَرُوا ... وَعَتَوْا ... وَقَالُوا ...) كأسلوب تسلسلي يوزع الأفعال ويشدُّ الانتباه إلى تتابع الفعل والعقوبة.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of the conjunction «wa» linking events (fa'qarū ... wa'ataw ... waqālū ...) functions as a sequential stylistic device that distributes actions and highlights the succession of acts and consequent blame.

claims.claim_ar: العبارة الشرطية/الاستفهامية «ائتِنَا بِمَا تَعِدُنَا إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ» تُقرأ قراءَةً بلاغيةً كاستفهام إنكاري أو تحدٍّ يضع الشكوك في مصداقية المرسل.
claims.claim_en: The conditional/ interrogative phrase «Bring us what you promise if you are of the messengers» is rhetorically read as a challenging/denying interrogative that casts doubt on the messenger's authenticity.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited source speaks of hamza-based rhetorical interrogation (همزة الاستفهام الإنكاري) in other contexts; mapping that discussion onto the conditional/if-clause «إن كنت» in this verse is interpretative and should be checked against specialized balagha discussions.

warnings: Provided source chunks are primarily i'rab/grammatical commentaries (Darwish) and contain illustrative examples rather than an explicit balagha treatment of S7:A77 by Jurjānī, Sakkākī, al-Baqillānī, al-Suyūṭī or dedicated tafsir-balagha. The source_quote_ar fields therefore point to grammatical/rhetorical examples in the chunks rather than direct citations of those classical balagha works.
